title: Cutting contest story with Joe and Russell Smith
summary: At a club, Joe Smith packed up his horn after Punch's solo; they discuss Joe and Russell Smith's playing styles.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Oh, yeah. Well, I got up, started to make a solo. Yeah. And there had a light. Let's light that light there. I didn't know nothing about the light, see. And I jumped up, took a solo, and that light went on to me. Yeah. I'd see me fogging going on. I never did that. But I did all right there. I did all good. And I never get a jam session. Some guy was standing outside, so I was playing at a place called The Bookstove. We had about four pieces. So Joe, Joe, Joe Smith and Russell Smith, two brothers. Yeah. Joe said, go get him. Russell and Russell said, no, I ain't gonna bother him. Louis said, you go get him, Joe. Joe said, I'm going to get him. And he went in. I blow so much horn, man. He packed up right in front of everybody in the place. Just pack his horn up left. Well, he was a beautiful-
I had to play. I had to play then.
He was a beautiful blues man, but I don't think he could have cut you all around then.
Well, him and his brother played with flutcher, you know.
Yeah, but his brother was more of a straight man.
Oh, his brother was a straight trumpet player, Russell.
Could he get off at all?
No. He was a straight horn.
